chapters.title: ʿĀṣim and his two transmitters
paragraphs: The reader: ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd al-Kūfī (d. 127 AH) is the fifth of the ten readers. He was a Successor who led the reciters of Kūfah after Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī. He read the Qurʾān to al-Sulamī, who had read to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and to Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, who had read to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.
Shuʿbah: Abū Bakr Shuʿbah ibn ʿAyyāsh al-Kūfī (95–193 AH). He read the whole Qurʾān to ʿĀṣim three times, five verses at a sitting.

Ḥafṣ: Abū ʿUmar Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān al-Asadī al-Kūfī (90–180 AH), ʿĀṣim's stepson and the most precise transmitter of his reading. ʿĀṣim told him that he had taught him what he read to al-Sulamī, and taught Shuʿbah what he read to Zirr.

The way: Everything here is by the way (ṭarīq) of the Shāṭibiyyah. The two transmitters share most of the uṣūl; scholars count about 520 words in which they differ. Where Shuʿbah is not mentioned, he reads as Ḥafṣ.
Ḥafṣ's own choice: In 30:54 Ḥafṣ reads the ḍād in two ways, with fatḥah as ʿĀṣim taught, ضَعْفٍ, and with ḍammah by his own choice, ضُعْفٍ.

chapters.title: Istiʿādhah and basmalah
paragraphs: Istiʿādhah: Recitation opens with seeking refuge, أَعُوذُ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ, and then the basmalah, بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ.

Joining the three: The istiʿādhah, the basmalah and the start of the sūrah may be read in four ways: stopping after each; joining all three; stopping after the istiʿādhah and joining the basmalah to the sūrah; or joining the istiʿādhah to the basmalah and stopping before the sūrah.
Start of a sūrah: The basmalah is read at the beginning of every sūrah except Sūrat al-Tawbah. ʿĀṣim counts it as the first āyah of al-Fātiḥah.

Between two sūrahs: Shuʿbah and Ḥafṣ always separate two consecutive sūrahs with the basmalah. Three ways of joining are allowed. The one way that is not allowed is to join the basmalah to the end of the first sūrah and then stop, because the basmalah belongs to the beginning of a sūrah.
Al-Anfāl and al-Tawbah: There is no basmalah between them. The reciter may stop and breathe (waqf), pause briefly without breath (sakt), or join them (waṣl).

chapters.title: Mīm al-jamʿ and the meeting of two sākin letters
paragraphs: Before a vowelled letter: The plural mīm that follows hāʾ, kāf or tāʾ is read sākinah, without ṣilah, by both transmitters: عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ (1:7), وَمِنْ ءَابَآئِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّٰتِهِمْ (6:87).
Before a sākin letter: The mīm takes a temporary ḍammah without ṣilah in connected reading and is sākinah when stopping: عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْقِتَالُ (2:216), مِنْهُمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ (3:110).

The hāʾ before the mīm: After a kasrah or a sākin yāʾ the hāʾ keeps its kasrah in every state, and only the mīm takes ḍammah before a sākin: بِهِمُ ٱلْأَسْبَابُ (2:166), عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقِتَالُ (2:246).

Two sākin letters: When two sākin letters meet between two words, ʿĀṣim gives the first a kasrah: قُلِ ٱدْعُوا۟ (17:110), قَالَتِ ٱخْرُجْ (12:31), أَنِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟. The exceptions are the wāw of the plural and mīm al-jamʿ, which take ḍammah, as in ٱشْتَرَوُا۟ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ (2:16), and the nūn of مِنْ, which takes fatḥah, as in مِنَ ٱللَّهِ. A madd letter before a sākin is dropped in pronunciation.

chapters.title: Hāʾ al-kināyah
paragraphs: General rule: The pronoun hāʾ of the third person masculine singular, when it stands between two vowelled letters, is read with ṣilah: its ḍammah is lengthened into a wāw and its kasrah into a yāʾ of two ḥarakāt, as in رَبِّهِۦ فَصَلَّىٰ (87:15). If a hamzat al-qaṭʿ follows, the ṣilah is lengthened four ḥarakāt like madd munfaṣil: مَالُهُۥٓ إِذَا (92:11).
Next to a sākin: There is no ṣilah when a sākin letter comes before or after the hāʾ: لَهُ ٱلْمُلْكُ, فِيهِ هُدًى (2:2).
Words both read alike: Both read ḍammah without ṣilah in يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ (39:7), and sukūn of the hāʾ in أَرْجِهْ (7:111, 26:36) and فَأَلْقِهْ إِلَيْهِمْ (27:28).

Shuʿbah's sukūn: Shuʿbah reads the hāʾ sākinah in يُؤَدِّهْ إِلَيْكَ (3:75, both), نُؤْتِهْ مِنْهَا (3:145, both; 42:20) and نُوَلِّهْ مَا تَوَلَّىٰ وَنُصْلِهْ جَهَنَّمَ (4:115). Ḥafṣ reads all of these with kasrah and ṣilah: يُؤَدِّهِۦٓ, نُؤْتِهِۦ, نُوَلِّهِۦ, وَنُصْلِهِۦ.
Wa-yattaqh (24:52): Shuʿbah reads kasrah of the qāf and sukūn of the hāʾ, وَيَتَّقِهْ. Ḥafṣ reads sukūn of the qāf and kasrah of the hāʾ without ṣilah, وَيَتَّقْهِ.

Ḍammah or kasrah: Ḥafṣ reads the hāʾ with ḍammah, without ṣilah, in وَمَآ أَنسَىٰنِيهُ (18:63) and عَلَيْهُ ٱللَّهَ (48:10), with a heavy lām in the Name. Shuʿbah reads both with kasrah, without ṣilah, أَنسَىٰنِيهِ and عَلَيْهِ ٱللَّهَ, with a light lām.
Fīhi muhānā (25:69): Ḥafṣ reads the hāʾ with ṣilah of two ḥarakāt although a sākin yāʾ precedes it, فِيهِۦ مُهَانًا. Shuʿbah reads a short kasrah without ṣilah, فِيهِ مُهَانًا.

chapters.title: Madd and qaṣr
paragraphs: Madd muttaṣil: When a hamzah follows a madd letter in the same word, both transmitters lengthen four ḥarakāt (tawassuṭ): جَآءَ, سُوٓءٍ, جِيٓءَ.

Madd munfaṣil: When the madd letter ends one word and the hamzah begins the next, they also lengthen four ḥarakāt by the Shāṭibiyyah: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا, وَأَمْرُهُۥٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ (2:275). The ṣilah of hāʾ al-kināyah before a hamzah is treated the same way.
Madd badal and līn: Madd badal is two ḥarakāt, as in ءَامَنُوا۟. A līn letter followed by a hamzah is not lengthened in connected reading: شَىْءٍ, سَوْءَةَ.
Stopping: Madd ʿāriḍ li-l-sukūn and the līn letter before the last letter may be read two, four or six ḥarakāt when stopping.
Madd lāzim: Six ḥarakāt, in words and in the opening letters: ٱلضَّآلِّينَ, الٓمٓ, نٓ. The ʿayn of كٓهيعٓصٓ (19:1) and عٓسٓقٓ (42:2) is read four or six.
Opening of Āl ʿImrān: Stopping on the mīm of الٓمٓ gives six ḥarakāt. Joining it to the Name of Allah (3:1–2) gives the mīm a fatḥah, with six or two ḥarakāt.

chapters.title: The hamzahs
paragraphs: Two hamzahs in one word: Both transmitters pronounce both hamzahs fully (taḥqīq): ءَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ (2:6), أَءِنَّا.
Aʾaʿjamiyy (41:44): Ḥafṣ reads the second hamzah with tashīl, between hamzah and alif. Shuʿbah reads two full hamzahs: ءَأَعْجَمِىٌّ.

Shuʿbah's added interrogative: Shuʿbah reads with two hamzahs, as a question, where Ḥafṣ reads one hamzah as a statement: ءَأَامَنتُمْ (7:123, 20:71, 26:49; Ḥafṣ ءَامَنتُمْ), أَئِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجْرًا (7:113; Ḥafṣ إِنَّ), أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلرِّجَالَ (7:81; Ḥafṣ إِنَّكُمْ), أَئِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ (56:66; Ḥafṣ إِنَّا) and ءَأَن كَانَ (68:14; Ḥafṣ أَن كَانَ).

Repeated interrogative: In the eleven passages where a question is repeated, such as أَءِذَا كُنَّا تُرَٰبًا أَءِنَّا (13:5), ʿĀṣim reads both parts as questions. The exception is 29:28, where Ḥafṣ reads the first as a statement, إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةَ, and Shuʿbah reads it as a question, أَئِنَّكُمْ. Both read the second (29:29) as a question.

Interrogative before the definite article: The hamzat al-waṣl is not dropped here. In ءَآلذَّكَرَيْنِ (6:143, 144), ءَآللَّهُ (10:59, 27:59) and ءَآلْـَٰٔنَ (10:51, 91), ʿĀṣim has two ways: ibdāl of the second hamzah into an alif of six ḥarakāt, or tashīl without madd.

Interrogative before a verb with hamzat al-waṣl: The hamzat al-waṣl is dropped and only the interrogative is read, in seven words, among them أَتَّخَذْتُمْ (2:80), أَطَّلَعَ ٱلْغَيْبَ (19:78) and أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ (38:75).
Two hamzahs in two words: Both are read with taḥqīq, whether their vowels agree or differ: جَآءَ أَحَدَكُمُ, يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ.

Sākin hamzah after hamzat al-waṣl: In connected reading the hamzah is pronounced. When beginning with the word, it is changed into a madd letter matching the vowel of the hamzat al-waṣl: ٱئْتُونِى is begun اِيتُونِى, and ٱؤْتُمِنَ (2:283) is begun اُوتُمِنَ.
Single hamzah: The general rule for both is taḥqīq, with no naql: يُؤْمِنُونَ, بِئْسَ, ٱلْأَرْضِ.
Huzuʾan and kufuʾan: Shuʿbah reads them with a hamzah, هُزُؤًا and كُفُؤًا (112:4). Ḥafṣ reads a wāw in place of the hamzah, هُزُوًا and كُفُوًا.
Murjaʾūna, turjiʾu, al-tanāʾush: Shuʿbah reads a hamzah in مُرْجَـُٔونَ (9:106), تُرْجِئُ (33:51) and ٱلتَّنَآؤُشُ (34:52). Ḥafṣ reads without it: مُرْجَوْنَ, تُرْجِى, ٱلتَّنَاوُشُ.

Luʾluʾ and muʾṣadah: Shuʿbah changes the first hamzah of لُؤْلُؤ into a wāw wherever it occurs, لُولُؤًا, and reads مُوصَدَةٌ (90:20, 104:8) without a hamzah. Ḥafṣ reads the hamzah in both, لُؤْلُؤًا and مُؤْصَدَةٌ.
Names: Shuʿbah reads جَبْرَئِلَ, مِيكَـٰٓئِيلَ and زَكَرِيَّآءَ, the last with a hamzah and madd muttaṣil. Ḥafṣ reads جِبْرِيلَ, مِيكَىٰلَ and زَكَرِيَّا.

chapters.title: Sakt
paragraphs: Ḥafṣ's four places: Ḥafṣ makes a short pause without breath, then continues, at عِوَجَا ۜ قَيِّمًا (18:1–2), مِن مَّرْقَدِنَا ۜ هَٰذَا (36:52), مَنْ ۜ رَاقٍ (75:27) and بَلْ ۜ رَانَ (83:14). This sakt is special to Ḥafṣ.

Shuʿbah in these places: Shuʿbah has no sakt and reads on. In the last two the ordinary rule of idghām applies, so he merges the nūn and the lām into the rāʾ: مَن رَّاقٍ and بَل رَّانَ, the latter with imālah.
Al-Ḥāqqah 69:28–29: When joining مَالِيَهْ to هَلَكَ, both transmitters have two ways: iẓhār of the first hāʾ with a brief sakt on it, which is preferred, or idghām of the first hāʾ into the second.

Hāʾ al-sakt: ʿĀṣim keeps the sākin hāʾ in both stopping and connected reading in seven words: يَتَسَنَّهْ (2:259), ٱقْتَدِهْ (6:90), كِتَٰبِيَهْ, حِسَابِيَهْ, مَالِيَهْ, سُلْطَٰنِيَهْ (Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah) and مَا هِيَهْ (101:10).

chapters.title: Idghām and iẓhār
paragraphs: Dhāl into tāʾ: Shuʿbah merges the dhāl into the tāʾ in every form of ٱتَّخَذتُّمُ and أَخَذتُّمْ, singular or plural. Ḥafṣ reads iẓhār: ٱتَّخَذْتُمُ (2:51), أَخَذْتُمْ (8:68).
Yā-Sīn and Nūn: When joining, Shuʿbah merges the nūn of the letter-name into the following wāw in يسٓ وَٱلْقُرْءَانِ (36:1–2) and نٓ وَٱلْقَلَمِ (68:1). Ḥafṣ reads iẓhār in both.
Yalhath dhālik and irkab maʿanā: Both transmitters merge the thāʾ into the dhāl in يَلْهَث ذَّٰلِكَ (7:176) and the bāʾ into the mīm in ٱرْكَب مَّعَنَا (11:42).

Agreed small idghām: Both merge the dhāl of إِذْ into dhāl and ẓāʾ, as in إِذ ظَّلَمُوٓا۟ (4:64); the dāl of قَدْ into dāl and tāʾ, as in قَد تَّبَيَّنَ (2:256); the feminine tāʾ into tāʾ, dāl and ṭāʾ, as in أُجِيبَت دَّعْوَتُكُمَا (10:89); and the lām of هَلْ, بَلْ and قُلْ into lām and rāʾ, as in بَل رَّفَعَهُ (4:158). Before the other letters these are read with iẓhār.

Incomplete idghām: The ṭāʾ is merged into the tāʾ while keeping its iṭbāq: أَحَطتُ (27:22), بَسَطتَ (5:28). In نَخْلُقكُّم (77:20) complete idghām of the qāf into the kāf is preferred, and incomplete idghām is also allowed.

Two vowelled letters: ʿĀṣim has no idghām kabīr. Both read مَكَّنِّى (18:95) with one doubled nūn, and لَا تَأْمَ۫نَّا (12:11) in two ways: ikhtilās of the ḍammah of the first nūn, or full idghām with ishmām.

chapters.title: Fatḥ and imālah
paragraphs: Ḥafṣ: Ḥafṣ reads with fatḥ throughout, except one word, the alif after the rāʾ in مَجْرَىٰهَا (11:41), which he reads with imālah.
Shuʿbah in that word: Shuʿbah reads it with ḍammah of the mīm and without imālah: مُجْرَىٰهَا.

Opening letters: Shuʿbah reads imālah in the rāʾ of الٓر and الٓمٓر, the hāʾ and yāʾ of كٓهيعٓصٓ, the ṭāʾ and hāʾ of طه, the ṭāʾ of طسٓمٓ and طسٓ, the yāʾ of يسٓ and the ḥāʾ of حمٓ. Ḥafṣ reads them all with fatḥ.
Shuʿbah's words: He reads imālah of the alif in أَدْرَىٰكَ and أَدْرَىٰكُم, رَمَىٰ (8:17), هَارٍ (9:109), أَعْمَىٰ (17:72), وَنَـَٔا (17:83) and رَانَ (83:14). In 41:51 he reads نَـَٔا with fatḥ.

Raʾā: Before a vowelled letter or a pronoun Shuʿbah reads imālah of both the rāʾ and the hamzah: رَءَا كَوْكَبًا (6:76), رَءَاهُ, رَءَاكَ. Before a sākin he reads imālah of the rāʾ only in connected reading, as in رَءَا ٱلْقَمَرَ (6:77) and رَءَا ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ (18:53); if he stops on the word, he reads imālah of both.
Suwan and sudan: Shuʿbah reads imālah only when stopping on سُوًى (20:58) and سُدًى (75:36); in connected reading the alif is dropped for the tanwīn.

chapters.title: Waqf
paragraphs: Anā and lākinnā: Both transmitters drop the alif of أَنَا۠ in connected reading and keep it when stopping. The same holds for لَّٰكِنَّا۠ (18:38).
Al-ẓunūnā, al-rasūlā, al-sabīlā (33:10, 66, 67): Shuʿbah reads the final alif both when stopping and in connected reading. Ḥafṣ drops it in connected reading and keeps it when stopping.

Salāsilā (76:4): Ḥafṣ reads the lām with fatḥah and no alif in connected reading; when stopping he may keep the alif or stop on a sākin lām. Shuʿbah reads tanwīn in connected reading, سَلَٰسِلًا, and stops on the alif.

Qawārīrā (76:15–16): Ḥafṣ reads both without alif in connected reading; he stops on the first with the alif and on the second with a sākin rāʾ. Shuʿbah reads both with tanwīn, قَوَارِيرًا, and stops on the alif.

Rawm and ishmām: ʿĀṣim, as one of the Kūfan readers, stops with rawm (a faint part of the vowel) on ḍammah and kasrah, and with ishmām (rounding the lips silently after the sukūn) on ḍammah only. Neither is used on fatḥah, on the feminine hāʾ, on mīm al-jamʿ, or on a temporary vowel.

Feminine tāʾ written open: ʿĀṣim follows the script and stops with a tāʾ on the words written with an open tāʾ, such as رَحْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ (2:218), نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ (2:231), ٱمْرَأَتُ عِمْرَٰنَ (3:35), and on يَٰٓأَبَتِ, مَرْضَاتِ, هَيْهَاتَ, وَلَاتَ, ٱللَّٰتَ and ذَاتَ.
Ayyuha: ʿĀṣim stops with a sākin hāʾ, without alif, on أَيُّهَ in 24:31, 43:49 and 55:31.

chapters.title: Yāʾāt al-iḍāfah
paragraphs: Meaning: The yāʾ of the first person attached to a noun, verb or particle is written in the muṣḥaf; the readers differ on reading it with fatḥah or sukūn.

Before hamzat al-qaṭʿ: Both transmitters generally read sukūn: إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ, مِنِّىٓ إِنَّكَ, وَإِنِّىٓ أُعِيذُهَا (3:36). Both read fatḥah in مَا لِىَ لَآ أَرَى (27:20) and وَمَا لِىَ لَآ أَعْبُدُ (36:22).

Ḥafṣ's fatḥah before a hamzah: Ḥafṣ reads fatḥah, and Shuʿbah sukūn, in مَعِىَ أَبَدًا (9:83), مَعِىَ أَوْ رَحِمَنَا (67:28), يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ (5:28), وَأُمِّىَ إِلَٰهَيْنِ (5:116) and أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا in its nine places (10:72; 11:29, 51; 26:109, 127, 145, 164, 180; 34:47). Where Shuʿbah reads sukūn before a hamzah, he lengthens the yāʾ four ḥarakāt as madd munfaṣil.

Before the definite article: Both read fatḥah, as in رَبِّىَ ٱلَّذِى (2:258), except عَهْدِى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ (2:124): Shuʿbah reads fatḥah, عَهْدِىَ, and Ḥafṣ reads sukūn, so the yāʾ drops in connected reading.
Before hamzat al-waṣl: Both read sukūn, as in أَخِى ٱشْدُدْ (20:30–31) and إِنِّى ٱصْطَفَيْتُكَ (7:144), except مِنۢ بَعْدِى ٱسْمُهُ (61:6): Shuʿbah reads fatḥah, بَعْدِىَ, and Ḥafṣ reads sukūn.

Before other letters: Ḥafṣ reads fatḥah, and Shuʿbah sukūn, in بَيْتِىَ (2:125, 22:26, 71:28), وَجْهِىَ (3:20, 6:79), مَعِىَ wherever it occurs, such as مَعِىَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ (7:105), and لِىَ in وَمَا كَانَ لِىَ (14:22, 38:69), وَلِىَ فِيهَا (20:18), وَلِىَ نَعْجَةٌ (38:23) and وَلِىَ دِينِ (109:6).
Agreed before other letters: Both read fatḥah in وَمَحْيَاىَ (6:162), and sukūn in وَمَمَاتِى (6:162), صِرَٰطِى مُسْتَقِيمًا (6:153) and أَرْضِى وَٰسِعَةٌ (29:56).

chapters.title: Yāʾāt al-zawāʾid
paragraphs: Meaning and general rule: These are final yāʾs that are pronounced by some readers but not written in the muṣḥaf. ʿĀṣim drops all sixty-two of them, both when stopping and in connected reading, as in ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ (2:186), with one exception for each transmitter.

Ḥafṣ's exception: In فَمَآ ءَاتَىٰنِۦَ ٱللَّهُ (27:36) Ḥafṣ reads a yāʾ with fatḥah in connected reading; when stopping he may keep it as a sākin yāʾ or drop it. Shuʿbah drops this yāʾ in both states: ءَاتَىٰنِ.
Shuʿbah's exception: In يَٰعِبَادِىَ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمُ (43:68) Shuʿbah reads a yāʾ with fatḥah in connected reading and a sākin yāʾ when stopping. Ḥafṣ drops it in both states: يَٰعِبَادِ.

chapters.title: Individual words in which Shuʿbah differs from Ḥafṣ
paragraphs: Words both read alike: Both transmitters read مَٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ (1:4) with alif, يُضَٰهِـُٔونَ (9:30) with hamzah, يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ with hamzah, أُسْوَةٌ (33:21) with ḍammah, وَخَاتَمَ (33:40) with fatḥah of the tāʾ, بِمُصَيْطِرٍ (88:22) with ṣād, and حَمَّالَةَ ٱلْحَطَبِ (111:4) with fatḥah.
Kasrah for ḍammah: Shuʿbah reads kasrah of the first letter in بِيُوت, ٱلْغِيُوبِ, عِيُون and شِيُوخًا; Ḥafṣ reads ḍammah: بُيُوت, ٱلْغُيُوبِ, عُيُون, شُيُوخًا.

Ḍammah for kasrah: Shuʿbah reads مُتُّمْ, مُتْنَا, مُتُّ and, in Sūrat Maryam, جُثِيًّا, عُتِيًّا, صُلِيًّا; Ḥafṣ reads مِتُّمْ, مِتْنَا, مِتُّ, جِثِيًّا, عِتِيًّا, صِلِيًّا. In Āl ʿImrān Ḥafṣ too reads مُتُّمْ. Shuʿbah reads رُضْوَٰن with ḍammah of the rāʾ everywhere except رِضْوَٰنَهُ (5:16); Ḥafṣ always reads kasrah.

Lighter and heavier forms: Shuʿbah reads خُطْوَٰتِ (Ḥafṣ خُطُوَٰتِ), رَءُفٌ without wāw (Ḥafṣ رَءُوفٌ), ٱلْمَيْتِ and مَيْتٍ (Ḥafṣ ٱلْمَيِّتِ, مَيِّتٍ), جُزُءًا (Ḥafṣ جُزْءًا), تَذَّكَّرُونَ (Ḥafṣ تَذَكَّرُونَ), تَلَقَّفُ (Ḥafṣ تَلْقَفُ; 7:117, 20:69, 26:45), تَسَّٰقَطْ (19:25; Ḥafṣ تُسَٰقِطْ), and مُبَيَّنَةٍ, مُبَيَّنَٰتٍ with fatḥah of the yāʾ (Ḥafṣ مُبَيِّنَةٍ, مُبَيِّنَٰتٍ).

Singular and plural: Shuʿbah reads the plural بِمَفَازَاتِهِمْ (39:61), مَكَانَاتِكُمْ, مَكَانَاتِهِمْ, بَيِّنَٰتٍ (35:40) and جِمَٰلَٰتٌ (77:33), where Ḥafṣ reads the singular بِمَفَازَتِهِمْ, مَكَانَتِكُمْ, مَكَانَتِهِمْ, بَيِّنَتٍ, جِمَٰلَتٌ. Shuʿbah reads the singular ءَايَةٌ (29:50) and ثَمَرَتٍ (41:47), where Ḥafṣ reads the plural ءَايَٰتٌ and ثَمَرَٰتٍ.

Verb prefixes: Ḥafṣ reads يَبْغُونَ and يُرْجَعُونَ (3:83), يَجْمَعُونَ (3:157), يُؤْتِيهِمْ (4:152), يَحْشُرُهُمْ (10:45), نُوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ (16:43) and تَسْتَطِيعُونَ (25:19). Shuʿbah reads تَبْغُونَ, تُرْجَعُونَ, تَجْمَعُونَ, نُؤْتِيهِمْ, نَحْشُرُهُمْ, يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِمْ and يَسْتَطِيعُونَ.
Qāla and qul: Ḥafṣ reads قَٰلَ رَبِّ ٱحْكُم (21:112) and قَالَ رَبِّى يَعْلَمُ (21:4); Shuʿbah reads قُل in both.

Case endings and tanwīn: Ḥafṣ reads مَعْذِرَةً (7:164), مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ (8:18), مَتَٰعَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ (10:23), مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ (11:40, 23:27), سَوَآءً (22:25), وَٱلْخَٰمِسَةَ (24:9), فَأَطَّلِعَ (40:37), بَٰلِغُ أَمْرِهِۦ (65:3) and نَزَّاعَةً (70:16). Shuʿbah reads مَعْذِرَةٌ, مُوهِنٌ كَيْدَ, مَتَٰعُ, مِن كُلِّ, سَوَآءٌ, وَٱلْخَٰمِسَةُ, فَأَطَّلِعُ, بَٰلِغٌ أَمْرَهُۥ and نَزَّاعَةٌ.
Thamūd: Both read وَثَمُودَا۟ without tanwīn in 53:51. In its three other places Shuʿbah reads tanwīn, ثَمُودًا, and Ḥafṣ reads without it.
Yā bunayya: Ḥafṣ reads يَٰبُنَىَّ with fatḥah everywhere. Shuʿbah reads fatḥah only in 11:42 and kasrah elsewhere, يَٰبُنَىِّ (12:5; 31:13, 16, 17; 37:102).

Other forms: Ḥafṣ reads ٱسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْأَوْلَيَٰنِ (5:107), دَأَبًا (12:47), وَرَجِلِكَ (17:64), لِمَهْلِكِهِم (18:59), مَهْلِكَ (27:49), كِسَفًا (26:187, 34:9), ٱلرَّهْبِ (28:32), لِّلْعَٰلِمِينَ (30:22), لَا مُقَامَ (33:13), بَـِٔيسٍ (7:165) and فَيُسْحِتَكُم (20:61). Shuʿbah reads ٱسْتُحِقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ, دَأْبًا, وَرَجْلِكَ, لِمَهْلَكِهِم, مَهْلَكَ, كِسْفًا, ٱلرُّهْبِ, لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ, لَا مَقَامَ, بَيْـَٔسٍ and فَيَسْحَتَكُم. Both read كِسَفًا in 17:92 and 30:48, and كِسْفًا in 52:44.
Niʿimmā: Shuʿbah reads the ʿayn of نِعِمَّا (2:271, 4:58) in two ways, with sukūn or with ikhtilās of its kasrah. Ḥafṣ reads a full kasrah.
Min ladunhu (18:2): Shuʿbah reads the dāl sākinah with ishmām of ḍammah, then kasrah of the nūn and of the hāʾ with ṣilah: مِن لَّدْنِهِۦ. Ḥafṣ reads مِن لَّدُنْهُ.

doubts: Wa-yattaqh (24:52): elibyari_asim.pdf p.26–27 counts it among words where Ḥafṣ has ṣilah and adds a garbled note about ḍammah of the hāʾ and a heavy lām; I followed rules_shuba_hafs.pdf p.14 (Ḥafṣ: sukūn of the qāf, kasrah of the hāʾ, no ṣilah).

Min ladunhu: elibyari_asim.pdf p.27–28 speaks of two words in al-Kahf (18:2 and 18:76 min ladunnī) and of two ways for the dāl (sukūn with ishmām, or ikhtilās of the ḍammah). The text is garbled; I wrote only the 18:2 reading with ishmām, which the quoted Shāṭibiyyah verse supports, and left out 18:76 and the ikhtilās option.
Sakt: elibyari_asim.pdf p.28 calls them 'the 3 obligatory' pauses yet lists four places, and gives Yā-Sīn 54 and al-Qiyāmah 37; rules_shuba_hafs.pdf p.21 gives 36:52 and 75:27, which I used.

Al-ẓunūnā, al-rasūlā, al-sabīlā: elibyari_asim.pdf p.39 says Ḥafṣ drops the alif both when stopping and in connected reading; rules_shuba_hafs.pdf p.24 says he drops it in connected reading and keeps it when stopping. I wrote the latter.

Madd: rules_shuba_hafs.pdf p.15 says four ḥarakāt for muttaṣil and munfaṣil by the Shāṭibiyyah and five by the Taysīr; elibyari_asim.pdf p.25 gives four only. I wrote four. The 2/4/6 for the letter ʿayn in elibyari p.56 belongs to its Ṭayyibah section, so I gave only 4 or 6 (rules_shuba_hafs.pdf p.16).
7:81: rules_shuba_hafs.pdf p.6 quotes it with the word al-fāḥishah; the word in that verse is al-rijāl (as in elibyari_asim.pdf p.41), which I used.
Mittum/muttum: elibyari_asim.pdf p.36 says ʿĀṣim (both) reads ḍammah in '3:173,174'; those numbers look wrong for this word (it occurs at 3:157–158), so I wrote only 'in Āl ʿImrān'.

elibyari_asim.pdf p.48–49 has a passage about ikhtilās in 4:153, 10:35 (yahiddī) and 36:48 and 'iskān' that does not clearly name the transmitter and seems to belong to another reader; I omitted it, including any Shuʿbah difference in 10:35 that the quoted Shāṭibiyyah verse may imply.

The word lists in elibyari_asim.pdf p.34–37 are badly garbled and mostly give word pairs without explanation; I supplied the vowelling of each pair for Ḥafṣ and Shuʿbah myself. Items I could not identify safely were left out (for example a word printed like 'malaṣā' near 19:51, and the verses on dakkāʾ and al-ṣudfayn quoted without an English statement). Words listed without a verse reference (jithiyyā/ʿitiyyā/ṣiliyyā, fa-yusḥitakum, 21:4, the names Jibrīl/Mīkāl/Zakariyyā, juzʾan, baʾīs) are given as I know the two readings; please verify.
Thamūd: elibyari_asim.pdf p.39 says Shuʿbah reads tanwīn in 'the 3 other places' without naming them; I did not add the references.
Fa-mā ātāniya (27:36) when stopping: elibyari_asim.pdf p.53 gives two ways for Ḥafṣ (sākin yāʾ or dropping); rules_shuba_hafs.pdf p.27 says keeping the yāʾ is preferred.

rules_shuba_hafs.pdf p.25 says Ḥafṣ stops with a yāʾ on hād, wāq, wāl and bāq; this looks like an error, so I omitted it, together with the other stopping details given only there (wayka'anna, māli, ayyan mā).
Baʾīs (7:165) and niʿimmā: the source gives a single Shuʿbah form for baʾīs and does not state Ḥafṣ's reading of niʿimmā; the Ḥafṣ forms are from the standard Ḥafṣ text.
General tajwīd sections of the sources that are identical for both transmitters and not specific to this qirāʾah (tafkhīm and tarqīq of rāʾ and lām, mīm sākinah) were left out.
